common_name: Abbeville Blue Chaste Tree (Louisiana Nursery True-Blue Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Abbeville Blue was selected in the early 1990s by the former Louisiana Nursery for unusually deep, true-blue flower spikes and a somewhat more cold-hardy constitution than many other named vitex selections.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or set out container-grown plants in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun. Abbeville Blue carries some of the truest, most saturated blue flower spikes among named chaste tree selections, opening 12-18 inch panicles on new wood from midsummer into fall above aromatic, palmately compound gray-green foliage with a silvery cast on the leaf undersides. It performs as a large multi-stemmed shrub in cooler parts of its range and can be trained into a small single- or multi-trunk tree in warmer zones, tolerating heat, drought, and poor soil once established while remaining largely untouched by deer. Cut the entire plant back hard to 12-18 inches above the ground each late winter to renew growth and maximize the length and density of the following summer's bloom spikes.

common_name: Salinas Pink Chaste Tree (Greg Grant Pink-Flowered Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Salinas Pink was selected by Texas plantsman Greg Grant for fragrant, soft pink flower spikes, a color break from the more common blue, purple, and white vitex selections.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Salinas Pink produces fragrant, soft pink flower spikes roughly 6-10 inches long that repeat through the summer on new growth, giving a softer, cottage-garden color option compared with the blue and purple tones typical of most named chaste tree selections. It shares the species' salt and drought tolerance, aromatic gray-green palmate foliage, and heavy pull on bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds through the long bloom season. Prune hard to 12-18 inches above ground in late winter each year to keep the plant a manageable size and encourage the densest flush of flower spikes the following summer.
sources: Stephen F. Austin State University Mast Arboretum
North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Delta Blues Chaste Tree (Compact Intermediate Blue-Flowered Vitex, First Editions PIIVAC-I)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Delta Blues (patented as PIIVAC-I under the First Editions brand) was bred as an intermediate-sized chaste tree, roughly two-thirds the mature size of a standard seedling vitex, for gardeners who want the bloom without the bulk.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun. Delta Blues was bred as a deliberately intermediate-sized chaste tree selection, reaching a rounded 8-10 feet tall and wide rather than the 15-20 foot spread of a typical seedling-grown vitex, which makes it easier to fit into foundation plantings and smaller residential beds while still delivering a long summer-into-fall display of deep bluish-purple, fragrant flower spikes. The aromatic gray-green palmate foliage and strong pull on bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds match those of full-size chaste tree selections, and the plant shares the same heat and drought tolerance once established. Prune back by roughly a third in late winter to maintain its compact rounded form and encourage the heaviest bloom the following season.
